subject: Deployment boundary & custody: Dedicated vs Private VPC — next steps
messages:

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-09-16T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Deployment boundary & custody: Dedicated vs Private VPC — post-call recap

Hi Marta / Raj —

Thanks for taking the time today — appreciate the clear framing on your data custody constraints. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Summary of what I heard from HealthSync
- Primary workloads will process PHI and must be logically and physically isolated from other tenants.
- You need control-plane residency inside your VPC or on-prem (for audit/compliance).
- Key management: customer-managed keys (BYOK/KMS) are required for encryption at rest.

Redwood options that map to your asks
- Hosted API: fastest to spin up, but control plane and data paths transit Redwood-managed services (not acceptable for PHI per your note).
- Dedicated capacity: dedicated GPU pools with network isolation and optional private peering; control plane still Redwood-hosted by default but we can offer a private control-plane arrangement for enterprises.
- Private VPC / on-prem: full control-plane residency inside your VPC (or on-prem appliance for air-gapped), meets the strongest custody requirements but needs procurement/ops lead time.

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Can you confirm whether HealthSync requires the control plane to be resident in your VPC (yes/no)? This determines whether Dedicated with private control-plane is sufficient, or we must pursue Private/on-prem.
2) Please share the SOC2 / security questionnaire answers you mentioned. Monica — can you follow up with the standard SOC2 evidence pack if they want Dedicated?
3) We’ll send a short network diagram + POC plan by EOD tomorrow for Dedicated with private peering so you have something concrete to review.

Attachments: placeholder for network diagram (will send).

Thanks —
Sergio
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0109

From: Marta Ruiz <m.ruiz@healthsync.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@healthsync.com>
Date: 2025-09-17T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Deployment boundary & custody: Dedicated vs Private VPC — post-call recap

Thanks, Sergio — good write-up. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Control plane: HealthSync requires the control plane to be resident inside our AWS account (not a Redwood-managed control plane). We also need audit logging forwarded to our SIEM.
- Data egress: PHI cannot leave our VPC (so any tokenized/cache material must remain inside).
- KMS: we must use our KMS with key rotation policies.

I’m attaching the SOC2 questions we run across vendors (partial answers included by our security lead). Please review and flag any absolute blockers.

We’re open to Dedicated if Redwood can commit to a private control-plane deployment inside our account; otherwise we will need the Private (VPC or on-prem) option. Cost is a factor but compliance is non-negotiable.

Subject: Re: Deployment boundary & custody: Dedicated vs Private VPC — technical notes and proposed artifacts

Hi Marta / Raj —

Thanks for the SOC2 questions — we reviewed the sheet and annotated a few items inline. Quick technical clarifications and what we can commit to for a Dedicated private control-plane arrangement: 

What Dedicated + private control-plane gives you (short):
- Dedicated GPU pools and tenant isolation at the runtime layer (no co-mingling of inference GPU processes).
- Private control-plane option: we can deploy our control plane components (management API, orchestration) into your AWS account using a restricted IAM role and private subnets. That gives you control-plane residency and auditability.
- Network egress: we will ensure all inference traffic (model payloads, KV cache) remains within your VPC via VPC endpoints and private peering.
- KMS: we support customer-managed KMS keys and can integrate with your rotation policies.

Differences vs Private (full VPC or on-prem) to note:
- Private (on-prem) gives you absolute isolation and no Redwood-managed surface; higher ops overhead and longer lead time (procurement + networking + on-site validation).
- Dedicated + private control-plane is typically faster to stand up and covers most compliance requirements, but some auditors prefer full Private deployment for PHI-heavy regulated customers.

Proposed immediate artifacts (attached)
- redwood-dedicated-network-diagram.pdf — proposed network layout for Dedicated with control plane deployed into your account.
- short POC checklist (I included target timeline: 4–6 weeks from kickoff, dependent on network approvals).

Ask / next steps
1) HealthSync: please confirm whether your procurement/legal team requires any additional contract language for private control-plane and BYOK (if so, share redlines).
2) Security: please send a point-of-contact and a preferred date/time for a short (30m) technical workshop next week so we can walk the diagram.
3) Sergio: I’ll prepare a canary plan and preliminary SLA language for Dedicated private control-plane.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call to walk through the diagram.

—Lauren
